channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Viewpoint Photographic Art Center — 2027 Call for Exhibit Proposals
item.description: Sacramento non-profit photography center seeking proposals for solo and group exhibitions running January–December 2027. Main Gallery proposals are open to all artists working in the photographic arts; the more intimate Step-Up Gallery is reserved for current Viewpoint members. Exhibits run roughly four weeks in both galleries. Submit a cohesive body of work — a representative selection of 20 images plus a short artist statement — reviewed by the Viewpoint Curatorial Committee. Maximum two proposals per artist; past solo exhibitors must wait three years before another solo show. — Deadline: June 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo or group exhibition (~4 weeks).

item.title: Fabula Works — Cycle(s)
item.description: Second open call from Rome curatorial platform Fabula Works, themed Cycle(s). Two photographers are selected for a fall exhibition at Millepiani in Rome (November 6 – December 22, 2026), with printing and exhibition promotion fully covered. All genres welcome; the jury seeks work that moves beyond familiar aesthetics with a distinct perspective. Guest juror is photographer Carolyn Mendelsohn (Nikon Europe Ambassador). Submit 10–25 photographs as a portfolio with biography and artist statement. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: €25. Prize: Exhibition (printing & promotion covered).

item.title: Still, Life · Photobook Cafe & Rapid Eye Darkroom
item.description: Quarterly open call from Photobook Cafe and Rapid Eye Darkrooms, themed Still, Life — exploring the tension between motion and pause, presence and aftermath, with guest judge Elliott Gunn. Open to amateur, emerging, and established photographers worldwide. 35 selected photographers are featured in a group exhibition and printed zine at The Photobook Cafe in London. Three Best in Show winners receive a complimentary group exhibition. Exhibition opening July 30, 2026. — Deadline: July 20, 2026. Fee: £25. Prize: Exhibition + zine publication.

item.title: Close-up Photographer of the Year 2026 (CUPOTY 8)
item.description: The 8th edition of CUPOTY, the international competition dedicated to close-up, macro, and micro photography. Eleven categories cover Animals, Insects, Invertebrate Portrait, Arachnids, Butterflies & Dragonflies, Underwater, Plants, Fungi & Slime Moulds, Intimate Landscape, Studio Art, and Young CUPOTY (under 18). The overall winner receives £2,500 plus a macro kit and trophy; category winners receive £250 each. Earlybird pricing runs to June 7; entries accepted up to a week after the July 12 deadline. — Deadline: July 12, 2026. Fee: £22 / £33 / £44 (6 / 15 / 30 images). Prize: £2,500 + macro kit; £250 per category.

item.title: Self — Carlotta Gallery
item.description: Carlotta Gallery's themed virtual exhibition on self-portraiture — a practice as old as photography itself. The call welcomes portraits that examine how one appears and how one is momentarily held by the camera, from literal self-portraits to conceptual approaches to identity and presence. Free to apply, pay only if selected; selected work is shown in a virtual exhibition for 6–12 months with catalogue, Collections-page listing, and certificate. — Deadline: July 10, 2026. Fee: Free (£20–£35 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Colours III — Carlotta Gallery
item.description: The third edition of Carlotta Gallery's themed virtual exhibition celebrating colour — work that engages with colour in bold, unexpected, and original ways, from saturated compositions to subtle tonal variations. Free to apply, pay only if selected; selected work is shown in a virtual exhibition for 6–12 months with catalogue, permanent Collections-page listing, and certificate. — Deadline: July 20, 2026. Fee: Free (£20–£35 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Intentional Unconventional — Experimental Photography & Video · Photo Cleveland
item.description: Photo Cleveland's avant-garde multimedia exhibition for work that breaks from conventional imagery and storytelling, favoring abstraction, non-linear structures, and unconventional techniques. The focus is on how an image was made rather than its subject — work where the artist pushed beyond traditional methods. Accepts photography, video, and mixed media (mixed media must have photography as its main component). Selected works are shown in a physical exhibition at The Brownhoist in Cleveland, opening Saturday July 11 (6–9 PM, with a live audio-visual installation by Ryan Kinney and Jim Szudy) and running July 11–31, 2026. No nudity (all-ages event); no religious or political themes. Artists may submit up to three works. — Deadline: June 27, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 works) / $20 (2 videos). Prize: Group exhibition at The Brownhoist, Cleveland.

item.title: New South, Volume III · Atlanta Center for Photography
item.description: Open call for the Atlanta Center for Photography's 2026 group publication, New South, Volume III — a self-published photo book featuring lens-based work made in, of, from, and about the American South. The 2025 edition featured over 81 artists. ACP frames the South broadly: defined by relationship and impact rather than personal Southern heritage, location, or 'quintessentially Southern' imagery. Open to emerging and established photographers; ACP especially encourages submissions from those who identify as Black, Indigenous, Latinx, Asian, LGBTQ+, and people with disabilities. Submit 1–5 images. Selected works appear in a high-quality 8x10 printed book (60 to 100+ pages), produced and sold through the ACP website, approved retailers, and in person in Atlanta by early October 2026. — Deadline: June 14, 2026. Fee: $15. Prize: Inclusion in printed group publication.

item.title: Space to Feel — SaveArtSpace Bus Shelter Exhibition
item.description: Public art exhibition on bus shelter advertising space in Miami, FL, curated by Leah Guzman, a board-certified art therapist and professional artist. The theme explores emotional honesty, tenderness, healing, and human connection — celebrating vulnerability and mental health through art. Open to all mediums, including photography, and to artists of all ages and backgrounds. Selected works are displayed on Miami bus shelters for at least one month starting August 14, 2026. SaveArtSpace is a non-profit that has run public art billboard and transit exhibitions since 2015; fees are structured as tax-deductible donations supporting exhibition production. — Deadline: June 29, 2026. Fee: $35 (1–3 images), $10 each additional. Prize: Public bus shelter exhibition (1+ month) in Miami.

item.title: Ode to Womanhood — SaveArtSpace Billboard Exhibition
item.description: Public art exhibition on billboard and bus shelter advertising space throughout New York City, curated by Ceres (Diaja), an award-winning photographer. The theme celebrates womanhood in all its authenticity, with emphasis on counterculture perspectives that challenge societal expectations around aging, career, marriage, and motherhood. Open to all mediums, including photography, and to artists of all ages and backgrounds. Selected works are displayed across NYC for at least one month starting August 7, 2026; artists are notified after July 6, 2026. SaveArtSpace is a non-profit that has run public art exhibitions since 2015; fees are tax-deductible donations supporting production. — Deadline: June 22, 2026. Fee: $35 (1–3 images), $10 each additional. Prize: Public billboard exhibition (1+ month) in NYC.

item.title: Home Is Where I Make It — SaveArtSpace Billboard Exhibition
item.description: Public art exhibition on billboard advertising space in New York City. The theme explores the experiences of making homes in unfamiliar places — celebrating how immigrants and their children build new rituals and communities. Open to artists of all ages and backgrounds; photography welcome. Selected works are displayed on NYC billboards for at least one month starting July 24, 2026. SaveArtSpace is a non-profit that has run public art billboard exhibitions since 2015; fees are structured as tax-deductible donations supporting exhibition production. — Deadline: June 8, 2026. Fee: $35 (1–3 images), $10 each additional. Prize: Public billboard exhibition (1+ month) in NYC.

item.title: The Open Road: Endless Horizons · International Photography Hall of Fame
item.description: International photography competition from the International Photography Hall of Fame and Museum (IPHF) marking the 100th anniversary of Route 66. Photographers worldwide are invited to reflect on the spirit of the open road — wanderlust, resilience, and discovery — in their own environments. Selected works are featured in an online exhibition at iphf.org. Awards: Grand Prize $1,000, First Place $500, Second Place $250, Third Place $100. Jurors: Susan Hacker Stang (photographer/educator), Shellee Graham (photographer and Route 66 ambassador), and Jim Ross (Route 66 historian). Open internationally to artists 18+; work must be original and not previously exhibited at IPHF. AI-generated or significantly AI-altered work is not eligible. — Deadline: June 21, 2026. Fee: Free members / $35 non-members. Prize: $1,000 grand prize + exhibition.

item.title: forgotten · A Smith Gallery
item.description: Online juried exhibition exploring the forgotten — abandoned, buried, erased, lost, repressed, bygone, neglected, vanished. Juror Ann Mitchell, a Southern California artist, curator, and educator (BFA Art Center College of Design, MFA Claremont Graduate University) whose work explores landscape, memory, and transformation. Up to 47 images selected; 27 featured in the hardbound "The 27" exhibition book. Awards: Juror's Award (online solo exhibition, book, blog feature), Directors' Award (book, blog feature), Visitors' Award ($100 for most Instagram likes). Exhibition July 31 – September 10, 2026 online, with reception August 29 at 3pm CST. — Deadline: July 6, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Personality: The Face and Its Absence · PH21 Gallery
item.description: Curated international group photography exhibition exploring personality and portraiture beyond the traditional face — through the body, objects, spaces, traces, absence, or symbolic associations. All creative photographic interpretations welcome, including AI-generated photo-based images. Curated by Zsolt Bátori (PhD; founder/director PH21 Gallery; Photolucida board member) and Borbála Jász (art historian; Photolucida juror). Curator's choice receives three free entries for future PH21 exhibitions; honorable mentions also recognized. Special rate for students, unwaged, and low-income economies (€15–20). Early bird deadline June 15 at reduced rates; final deadline June 22. Exhibition at PH21 Gallery in Barcelona's Gothic Quarter, August 22 – September 15, 2026. — Deadline: June 22, 2026. Fee: €25–€50. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: DECAY, CORROSION, RUST · New York Center for Photographic Arts
item.description: Themed juried call for photography of decay, corrosion, and rust — abandoned buildings, rusted vehicles, peeling paint, junkyards — in any photographic medium. Cash prizes total $4,000 across ten awards: $1,100 Grand Prize, three First Prizes of $400, three Second Prizes of $325, three Third Prizes of $250, plus 20 Juror Selections and 20 Honorable Mentions. Juried by Darren Ching, co-owner of Klompching Gallery, New York. Winners featured in the NYC4PA online gallery and catalog with certificates; the winning image appears on the NYC4PA homepage. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers; 2-D work only. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: $4,000.

item.title: 2026 Portrait Award · The Independent Photographer
item.description: The Independent Photographer's monthly themed competition cycle, this round dedicated to portrait photography. Total prize pool $2,700: 1st prize $1,000, 2nd $600, 3rd $400, plus seven $100 finalist prizes. Winners exhibited in London and featured to the platform's 970k+ Instagram following. All entrants receive a free online portfolio. Judge: Luisa Dörr, the Brazilian photographer known for her portrait work. Submissions are tiered: $15 for 1 image, $30 for 3, $45 for 6. AI-generated work not accepted; photography-based submissions only. JPEG or PNG, minimum 1200px longest side, maximum 10MB. — Deadline: June 30, 2026. Fee: $15–$45. Prize: $2,700 pool.

item.title: The Sweep of Time: Beyond the Horizon
item.description: A call open to all traditional and non-traditional photographic and light-based media, including mixed media with a dominant lens-based component, presented as a participating venue project of the 2026 FotoFocus Biennial, The Long View. Invites work engaging time as subject, symbol, or environment; the horizon as literal landscape or conceptual threshold; and distance, duration, memory, or continuity. Every exhibiting artist receives a $50 honorarium; one work each exhibition period receives a $1,000 Grand Jury Award. Artists receive 70% on sales. Submit up to 3 entries for $45, $5 per additional. Exhibition at Manifest Gallery in Cincinnati, September 25 – October 23, 2026, launching the gallery's 23rd season. — Deadline: June 28, 2026. Fee: $45. Prize: $1,000.

item.title: Open 2026 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: Open-themed international photography exhibition — any genre, any subject. Selected work is shown in a month-long gallery exhibition in Glasgow (7–31 October 2026), with work also appearing in an online gallery and exhibition catalogue. All participants are put forward for Photographer of the Month consideration. Prints are produced on photographic paper and framed in gallery frames; photographers retain all copyright. Open to emerging and established photographers, professional and amateur, Scottish and international. Submit up to 8 JPEGs (300ppi minimum, 3000 pixels on shortest side) via free file-transfer to the gallery email. — Deadline: June 19, 2026. Fee: Free (£48 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Time 2026 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: International photography exhibition on the theme of time — the speed at which an image is captured, the passage of time, and how time changes places and people. Selected work is shown in a month-long gallery exhibition in Glasgow (7–31 October 2026), with work also appearing in an online gallery and exhibition catalogue. All participants are put forward for Photographer of the Month consideration. Prints are produced on photographic paper and framed in gallery frames; photographers retain all copyright. Open to emerging and established photographers, professional and amateur, Scottish and international. Submit up to 8 JPEGs (300ppi minimum, 3000 pixels on shortest side) via free file-transfer to the gallery email. — Deadline: June 19, 2026. Fee: Free (£48 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Der Greif × Fondament — I Spy With My Little Eye
item.description: Open call from Der Greif in collaboration with Fondament on the theme "Ich seh' etwas, was du nicht siehst" (I Spy With My Little Eye), exploring social life in Germany through photographs that tell more than one story and leave room for different readings. The brief asks for images that hold the tension between perception and interpretation rather than offering a single narrative. Selected work is featured in an exhibition. Free to enter via Picter. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Pine Meadow Ranch 2027 Artist Residency
item.description: Two- or four-week residency at Pine Meadow Ranch in Sisters, Oregon, run by the Roundhouse Foundation on a working ranch in the high desert of central Oregon. The 2027 program theme is "Process and Material." Open to many disciplines — photography (digital) is explicitly eligible alongside painting, ceramics, printmaking, fiber, sculpture, mixed and digital media, writing, music, performance, and creative research. A cohort of two to four residents shares a historic home, each with a private bedroom and a private studio adapted to their medium; residencies run March through mid-November. Provides a $200/week stipend plus up to $300 travel reimbursement for residents living more than 1,000 miles away. No application or residency fees. Applications are evaluated by panels of external reviewers; finalist interviews in mid-August, decisions announced September 2026. — Deadline: July 6, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 2–4 week residency + $200/week stipend.

item.title: The Surreal · TCG Gallery
item.description: International open call exploring surrealism — the human psyche, dreams, and the unconscious mind through bizarre, symbolic imagery. Open to all two-dimensional photographic work, traditional to non-conventional and alternative processes. Online exhibition July 1 – August 1, 2026. Blind jury; Curator's Choice, Director's Choice, and Honorable Mentions awarded. — Deadline: June 25, 2026. Fee: $15. Prize: Exhibition + awards.

item.title: Put a Pin(hole) In It · Blue Moon Camera & Machine
item.description: Group show of pinhole photography at Blue Moon Camera & Machine in Portland, Oregon, open to long-time pinhole enthusiasts and recent converts alike. Each photographer may submit up to 5 images (series welcome; the jury may select single images from a series). 25 works are curated from all submissions. Selected images must be delivered matted — not framed — in 16×20 mats (horizontal or vertical), and can be any size within the mat. Submitted files should be at least 1000px and no more than 3000px on the long edge, and include the photographer's name, contact info, and which pinhole camera was used. The show opens August 1, 2026. — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Stove Works Artist Residency 2027
item.description: One- to three-month residency in Chattanooga, Tennessee, open to artists across all disciplines including photography, as well as non-object-based practitioners such as writers, curators and academics. Eight residents are hosted between February and November 2027. Once accepted, the residency is free to attend: residents receive a private studio/bedroom with bathroom, shared kitchen, living space and laundry, and 24-hour access to on-site metal, wood and print shops plus a library. Programming includes visiting critics and open studios. Residents cover their own travel, materials and food. A $100 refundable security deposit and one inscribed book donation to the library are required on acceptance. International applicants welcome. The application fee is tiered: $10 (May 15–31), $20 (June 1–7), $30 (June 8–15). — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: $10–30. Prize: Free 1–3 month residency.

item.title: Form Photo Award / SCOPE Miami 2026
item.description: Contemporary photography prize with an open theme, accepting single images and series. Top 4 winners exhibit at the SCOPE Art Fair in Miami in December 2026 during Miami Art Week; shortlisted artists are published in Form Magazine. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: €35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Metamorfosi Residency 2026 · Italian Cultural Institute Prague
item.description: Artist residency in Prague run by the Italian Cultural Institute (IIC Prague) in collaboration with MUNAF — National Museum of Photography. One Italian artist is invited to develop a visual arts project under the theme Metamorphosis — reflecting on change and transformation across artistic practice and cultural context, with research open in theme and medium. The residency takes place at the IIC Prague guest house between autumn 2026 and spring 2027, lasting three to four weeks, structured in a planning phase and a production phase, and concluding with a public presentation. The total grant is €5,000 net, covering the artist's fee, all travel to and from the residency plus research travel, meals and accommodation at the guest house for the full stay, and production costs for the work delivered. Open to Italian artists with no age restriction. Apply by email with the application form, ID, CV and portfolio, a presentation of one completed project, a motivation letter, and the data-processing consent form. — Deadline: June 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Residency (€5,000 grant).

item.title: Folk House Darkroom Residency 2026
item.description: Darkroom residency at Bristol Folk House Darkroom, a community darkroom in central Bristol working towards more sustainable photographic processes. The residency is aimed at photographers and artists using or wanting to explore experimental, sustainable, and alternative processes — past residents have done work such as making developers from oats. Dates and length are flexible and chosen by the resident based on the darkroom's term schedule. Residents receive a stipend, darkroom training, darkroom space and equipment, and discounts in the Folk House café and programme. Open internationally; apply by email. — Deadline: June 22, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Residency.

item.title: Solo Exhibition July 2026 · All About Photo
item.description: Monthly featured photographer showcase. Winner receives a full month online solo exhibition (July 1–31, 2026), permanent gallery presence, exclusive interview, social media promotion, newsletter feature, international press coverage, and commission-free sales. Submit a cohesive project or portfolio of 6–14 images. — Deadline: June 23, 2026. Fee: $45. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: BINNAR Festival 2026
item.description: Multidisciplinary festival in Vila Nova de Famalicão, Portugal, running since 2016 with municipal support. Open call for the November 2026 edition welcomes photography and video for a collective exhibition with free theme. BINNAR handles all production: selected photos are printed and framed at no cost to the artist; videos must not exceed 2 minutes. Submissions are open internationally — artists send name, nationality, age, an artist statement and biography, plus a direct link to view the work, by email to info.binnar@gmail.com with subject line 'open call'. — Deadline: June 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition (production covered).

item.title: RED · Dusk Gallery
item.description: Themed exhibition at Dusk Gallery in Santa Fe celebrating bold uses of red in photography — images where red commands the frame. Documentary, fine art, abstract, and experimental approaches all welcome. Juried by Dusk founder Holly Hart. Selected photographers receive complimentary professional printing and framing in 24×24 inch black museum-quality frames with matting; the artist supplies only the high-resolution JPEG (500KB–5MB, 4500px on the longest side). The gallery adjusts file dimensions for presentation without cropping. Exhibition runs August 7–28, 2026 in Santa Fe. Sales split 50/50; selected images retained in the gallery's flat files for six months post-exhibition. Open worldwide. — Deadline: June 25, 2026. Fee: $40–$45. Prize: Exhibition + professional printing & framing.

item.title: A Celebration of Contemporary Photography · PhotoPlace Gallery
item.description: International juried exhibition at PhotoPlace Gallery in Middlebury, Vermont, programmed around World Photography Day (August 19). The call welcomes any subject, style, or process — landscape, portraiture, documentary, experimental, alternative process. Up to 35 images selected for the physical gallery exhibition, plus 40 additional images for the online exhibition; all 75 selected works appear in a printed catalog and remain permanently on the gallery's website. Awards include a Juror's Award ($300), Director's Award ($200), and three Honorable Mentions ($50 each). Juried by Paula Tognarelli (retired Executive Director, Griffin Museum of Photography) and Zach Hoffman (Gallery Owner/Director). Fully AI-generated work is not eligible. Exhibition runs August 7–29, 2026; prints due July 24. — Deadline: June 8, 2026. Fee: $39 (5 images) + $6 each additional. Prize: $300 + $200 + 3×$50 + exhibition + catalog.

item.title: A Show of Hands · Blue Sky Gallery
item.description: Online exhibition organized by Blue Sky, Oregon Center for the Photographic Arts, as part of its 50th anniversary programming. The brief invites photographers to interpret the hand as a subject — symbols of connection, expression and care; intimate gestures or collective movements. Curated by a Blue Sky committee. The exhibition launches July 2, 2026 on the gallery's website. Submission via Google Form: up to three images per artist, max 1500 pixels on the long edge, filename format lastname_firstname_title.jpg. Membership not required. Accepted works display online only and are not available for sale. Free to enter. — Deadline: June 12, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Innovate Grants - Spring $1,800 Grants
item.description: Two $1,800 quarterly grants for visual artists and photographers. Eighteen honorable mentions also featured on the Innovate platform (nine in art, nine in photo). No artist statement, project proposal, or letters of recommendation required. — Deadline: June 18, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: $1,800.

item.title: ENDLESS SUMMER Photography Exhibit · Decode Gallery
item.description: Themed exhibition at Decode Gallery in Tucson exploring summer's endless quality — golden hour on repeat, the weight of humid air, days that never seem to darken. Open to all photographic styles and approaches; not restricted to black-and-white. Twenty-six images are juried for the group exhibition by Decode founder Holly Hart, a conceptual fine art photographer. Selected artists receive complimentary professional printing on Epson Ultra Premium Luster paper and museum-quality 22×22 inch framing with precut mats; the artist supplies only the high-resolution JPEG. Exhibition runs September 5–26, 2026. Sales split 50/50 between gallery and artist; selected prints retained in the gallery's flat files for six months post-exhibition for further promotion. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. — Deadline: July 24, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 100 Book Award 2026 · Kult Books
item.description: Open call from Kult Books, an independent publishing project in Stockholm run by Janne Riikonen. One or two selected projects are produced as a published photobook in a limited edition of 100 copies, fully designed by the publisher, with an ISBN, catalogued and distributed via book fairs, online retailers, and bookshops. Selected artists receive 3 free copies and the option to purchase up to 20 additional copies at a 60% discount. Open to artists working primarily with photography in any style; supplementary media like drawing or writing may be incorporated as long as photography remains dominant. AI-generated work is not accepted. Submit 80–300 low-resolution JPGs via download link or a dummy/PDF with a work description by email to hello@kultbooks.com with 'open call' in the subject line. Results announced June 26, 2026; publication Spring 2027. — Deadline: June 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Photobook publication (100 copies) + 3 free copies.

item.title: PLAYA Art/Sci Awarded Residency 2027
item.description: Awarded residencies at PLAYA, a residency program in Lake County, Oregon, on traditional Klamath, Modoc, and Yahooskin Paiute lands. Photographers are welcome under the visual arts track. The 2027 cycle offers four jury-selected session options: January 21–February 15 (25 nights), February 18–March 1 (11 nights), July 15–August 2 (18 nights), and October 28–November 15 (18 nights). Residents receive free housing in 1- or 2-bedroom cabins with kitchens and bathrooms, studio/workspace access, and one shared group meal per week. No artist stipend; residents cover their own travel, meals beyond the group dinner, and materials. The program brings together artists and scientists across disciplines for cross-disciplinary exchange — selection criteria emphasize connection to science, especially related to Lake County's natural assets, and alignment with PLAYA's mission. Open globally to applicants 18+. Application fee $40 with full waivers available upon request. Decisions announced by October 1, 2026. Reference forms due July 19, 2026. — Deadline: June 30, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: 11–25 night residency + cabin + studio access.

item.title: Paris Photo–Aperture PhotoBook Awards 2026
item.description: Annual photobook awards co-presented by Aperture and Paris Photo, recognizing excellence across three categories: First PhotoBook ($10,000), PhotoBook of the Year, and Photography Catalog of the Year. Submission window opens June 10, 2026 (early-bird fees through July 10) and closes September 4, 2026 at 5pm EDT. Books must be published between September 2025 and September 2026. Submit via Picter alongside one physical copy mailed to Aperture in New York. Shortlist announced October 2026; winners revealed at Paris Photo on November 13, 2026. — Deadline: September 4, 2026. Fee: $15–$60. Prize: $10,000 First PhotoBook + 35 shortlist slots.

item.title: URBAN Photo Awards 2026
item.description: 17th edition of the international urban photography contest paired with Trieste Photo Days festival. Categories include Single Photos (Streets, People, Spaces, Creative), Projects & Portfolios, and an Under-35 track (free). Single Photos: first image free, up to 3 images €20, each additional €10. Projects & Portfolios: €40 per project. Category winners receive Giorgio Celiberti trophies (~€1,500 value), exhibits at Trieste Photo Days (October 23–25, 2026), 2-night Trieste stay for two with gala dinner, and partner photography prizes. 2026 jury presidents: Mark Power (Magnum) chairs Projects & Portfolios; Christopher Morris (VII Photo Agency) chairs Single Photos. — Deadline: June 14, 2026. Fee: Free first image, then €20+. Prize: Trophy + Trieste exhibition + 2-night stay.

item.title: TOKAS International Creator Residency Program 2027
item.description: Three-month residency in Tokyo run by Tokyo Arts and Space (TOKAS), the contemporary art programming arm of the Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo (MOT). Open to international visual artists (photographers welcome), designers, and architects with at least five years of professional experience. Six positions across three periods: May–July 2027, September–November 2027, and January–March 2028. Each resident receives round-trip airfare, a single-room studio apartment at TOKAS Residency in Koto-ku, shared workspace, a per diem of 4,200 JPY/day (approximately €25/$28), and a 300,000 JPY (≈€1,800/$2,000) creative work fee. Two letters of recommendation required. Applicants must not be students at the time of residency; previous TOKAS participants may reapply only for a program they have not completed. Application via online form plus uploaded PDF application form and portfolio. — Deadline: June 16, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: ¥300,000.

item.title: The Art of Experimentation — Symposium on Alternative Photography · Women Alternative Photography Group
item.description: Free open call for speakers and presenters for The Art of Experimentation, a one-day symposium on alternative photography dedicated to women, non-binary, and trans artists, researchers, and practitioners. Held in person at Bristol Folk House Darkroom on August 1, 2026 (10am–3pm). Co-organized by Women Alternative Photography Group and Folk House Darkroom. Three submission categories: 10–15 minute artist talk or research paper, 10–15 minute performance, or 10–15 minute film screening. Speakers receive an equal split of all ticket-sale proceeds; programme also includes a photo walk around Bristol and an informal show-and-tell where presenters can share physical work. Particularly welcomes students and emerging to mid-career applicants; commitment to inclusivity across race, ability, and experience. International applicants welcome but no travel funding or visa sponsorship provided. Submit a title, abstract (max 250 words), artist bio (max 100 words), category selection, and up to three images/films/performance documentation via online form. — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Speaker slot + payment.

item.title: Artadia Awards 2026 — Boston
item.description: Unrestricted merit-based grants for contemporary visual artists including photographers. Three awardees receive $15,000 each. Two-round jury process: curators review applications, then conduct 45-minute virtual studio visits with 6 finalists. Non-selected finalists receive honorariums. Eligibility restricted to artists living and working in Bristol, Essex, Middlesex, Norfolk, Plymouth, or Suffolk Counties (Massachusetts) for at least two consecutive years. Cannot be enrolled in an art degree program or have previously received Artadia awards of $10,000 or more. Application window: August 15 – September 15, 2026. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $15,000.

item.title: Artadia Awards 2026 — Atlanta
item.description: Unrestricted merit-based grants for contemporary visual artists including photographers. Three awardees receive $15,000 each. Two-round jury process: curators review applications, then conduct 45-minute virtual studio visits with 6 finalists. Non-selected finalists receive honorariums. Eligibility restricted to artists living and working in 23 Georgia counties — including Fulton, DeKalb, Cobb, Gwinnett, Cherokee, Clayton, Coweta, Fayette, Forsyth, Henry, and Rockdale — for at least two consecutive years. Cannot be enrolled in an art degree program or have previously received Artadia awards of $10,000 or more. Application window: September 1 – October 1, 2026. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $15,000.

item.title: Artadia Awards 2026 — Houston
item.description: Unrestricted merit-based grants for contemporary visual artists including photographers. Three awardees receive $15,000 each. Two-round jury process: curators review applications, then conduct 45-minute virtual studio visits with 6 finalists. Non-selected finalists receive honorariums. Eligibility restricted to artists living and working in Harris County, Texas for at least two consecutive years. Cannot be enrolled in an art degree program or have previously received Artadia awards of $10,000 or more. Application window: October 1 – November 1, 2026. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $15,000.

item.title: RED Photography Exhibit · Dusk Gallery
item.description: Juried photography exhibition celebrating red commanding the frame — documentary, fine art, abstract, and experimental styles welcome. 26 images selected for in-person exhibition at Dusk Gallery in Santa Fe, August 7–28, 2026. Gallery covers professional Luster-paper printing, matting, and 24×24 black museum-quality framing — artists submit JPEG only. 50% commission on any sales; photographers retain all rights. Prints archived in gallery flat files for six months post-exhibition. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. Juror: Holly Hart. — Deadline: June 25, 2026. Fee: $40–$45. Prize: Exhibition + free printing/framing.

item.title: The Abstract Vision
item.description: Virtual juried exhibition by SEC4P seeking non-representational photography — work that doesn't attempt to represent external reality but engages with shape, form, color, and texture. Source material may be nature, man-made, or figurative, but the resulting image must read as abstract. Black-and-white or color, analog, digital, and antique processes all welcome. Juror: Catherine Fairchild (Houston-based fine art photographer specializing in abstract work). 35–40 images selected for the virtual gallery; one-month online exhibition with social media promotion, archived slideshow, and video walkthrough. 0% commission — artists retain 100% of sale proceeds and copyrights. Open globally to photographers regardless of location, age, or skill level. — Deadline: July 15, 2026. Fee: $28–$35. Prize: Exhibition (0% commission).

item.title: Eidolon Grant 2026
item.description: Third edition of the Eidolon Grant from the Budapest-based Eidolon Centre for Everyday Photography, the only international platform dedicated to vernacular and everyday photography. €25,000 total prize pool distributed across two categories: (1) contemporary everyday photographic cultures (digital and social media imaging) and (2) everyday photographs of the past (19th-20th century vernacular archives). Number of winners determined by jury based on the applications received; payment in 3-4 installments. Open globally to artists, academics, researchers, enthusiasts, professionals, and collectors with no geographic restrictions; individual or group applications welcome. Application via Typeform with abstract (2,000 characters max), CV, project overview PDF (3 pages max), detailed project description PDF (10 pages max), and budget using the official Excel template. Submissions in English only. Call opens May 1, 2026; winners announced November 10, 2026. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €25,000 pool.

item.title: AOP OPEN 2026 · Association of Photographers
item.description: 16th edition of the Association of Photographers' international open award. No categories, no themes — open to professional, emerging, and amateur photographers. Single image, series (2–5 images), and moving image entries accepted. Innovative work using AR, VR, CGI or other techniques is eligible if created by a person. Judged by a panel of leading industry professionals — photographers, commissioners, curators, and specialists. Gold and Silver awards may be given in each format. Best in Show wins £1,250 plus a Fujifilm X Series kit (worth £1,500) and a 1-year Capture One Studio subscription. Gold and Silver winners receive AOP Photographer Membership and Capture One subscriptions. Selected finalists and winners exhibited at the Fujifilm House of Photography in early 2027. All images must have been created on or after 1 January 2024. — Deadline: June 8, 2026. Fee: £15 / £20 single (member / non-member). Prize: £1,250 + Fujifilm kit + exhibition.

item.title: Water ~ Sky · Praxis Photo Arts Center
item.description: Landscape photography exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis exploring the relationship between water and sky as elemental forms in landscape practice. The call seeks work that engages surface and depth, presence and distance, observation and sensation — sea, river, ocean, puddle, sky, cloud, weather, motion, horizon. All approaches welcome from documentary to conceptual. Thirty images selected for in-person exhibition at Praxis Gallery, July 18 – August 8, 2026. Open internationally. — Deadline: June 21, 2026. Fee: $35 (5 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: Exhibition + Juror's Choice + Directors' Choice.

item.title: Bay Area Photography Open Exhibition 2026 · The Image Flow
item.description: Second annual juried exhibition by The Image Flow (Mill Valley, CA) showcasing photographic artists in the extended San Francisco Bay Area. Open theme — all subject matter and media explorations eligible including digital, alternative processes, and analog. AI-generated images excluded. Restricted to photographers in nine Bay Area counties: Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Solano, and Sonoma. Jurors: Ann Jastrab, Nelson Chan, and Nathan Lomas. Selected work shown in a group exhibition with reception at The Image Flow gallery; online showcasing; softcover catalog produced. — Deadline: July 5, 2026. Fee: $40 (up to 3 images). Prize: Group exhibition + catalog.

item.title: The Print Center 101st ANNUAL International Competition
item.description: The Print Center's 101st edition of its long-running annual international competition for artists working with photography and/or printmaking. Open to local, national, and international artists; work must have been completed within the last three years. Up to five images or videos per submission. Selection produces 25 Semifinalists and 10 Finalists; three Finalists are given Solo Exhibitions at The Print Center (January-March 2027). Acquisition awards include the Philadelphia Museum of Art Collection Award and the Art Museum of West Virginia University Purchase Award via the Beth and Joe Hestick Acquisitions Fund. Additional cash prizes up to $1,000 and material awards from Awagami Paper. Jurors: Pepe Coronado (Director and Master Printer, Coronado printstudio, Austin) and Shana Lopes (Assistant Curator of Photography, SFMOMA). Notifications by September 11, 2026. — Deadline: June 18, 2026. Fee: $45. Prize: $1,000 + Exhibition.
